^  Mind.     iLoss  of  consciousness  and  frothing  from  mouth.

I  Hallucinations  of  sight,  smell  and  taste.

I I  Children  wake  up  in  evening  or  before  midnight  with
fear  or  fright,  jump  up,  see  sights,  scream,  tremble  and

I  Delirium  and  crying  out.

I  Child  is  whining  and  complaining;   very  restless  even

during  sleep ;  it  will  not  lie  awake  five  minutes  without

■  Fretting  excites  the  cough.

CINCHONA  OFFICINALIS  (<'hma).

Peruvian  Bark.  Rubiacese.

Unknown  previous  to  middle  of  seventeenth  century.  Named  from  Countess
El-Cinchon,  wife  of  the  vice  king  of  Peru.  It  was  distributed  by  the  Jesuits
among  the  poor  as  a  febrifuge.  Grows  on  eastern  range  of  Andes,  and  is  being
naturalized  in  India,

It  was  first  proved  by  Hahnemann  in  1790.

The  yellow  bark  was  mainly  used  in  the  provings.  Those  chiefly  used  in
pharmacy  are:  1.  Cinchona  Calisaya,  also  called  Cinchona  Eegia  or  Cinchona
Flava,  Koyal  or  genuine*  yellow  bark.  2.  Cinchona  de  Huanuco,  grey  or  silver
Cinchona ;  and,  3.  Cinchona  Rubra,  or  Ked  Cinchona.

Hahnemann  mentions  that  in  1790,  when  proving  Cortex  China,  the  first  idea
of  the  homoeopathic  law  of  cure  dawned  upon  his  mind.

For  provings,  see  Allen's  Encyclopedia,  v.  3.
